items.title: Lee Collins Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: It was going to be Joe Oliver and myself in the old plantation. So, and another corned player because they had a big show. Bob Schaffner, we'll use three corneds.

ctx.x: Yeah, and where was your job?

Yeah, they was working down there and there. Where was Joe playing then? Joe was playing in Lincoln Garden. Lincoln Garden. Louis was working at the Dreamland, and joined the band at the Dreamland. I mean Lil was working there together. So I come to Chicago and I joined Joe's band. Well Joe had George Fields and he had a big band. He had the kind of band that he had now. He had a corner player playing with a man by the name of Bob Schaffner. He went later to the plantation with Dave Payton. So with the band…
So I said, when did y'all go home?

items.title: Bob Shoffner Interview, 1959-09-08
items.q: he got her, Lee Collins and worked with me.

ctx.x: Mason, and he's in St. Louis now. Yeah.

Well that's what fate wanted me to come over. Well see by me playing that way that's where I come to know all those fellas and get their style because see when they come to like playing shows or hard music, they'd all the time say well Bob you take the lead trumpet. You can read it right off. Well I can read it well but then by playing beside them that's where I come to get the whole style. And of course I liked that style and was brought up with it. Well then I came up back in Chicago in 22 after leaving…
